learning_outcomes.text: explain the terminology of Human-Machine Interaction and its basic concepts, as well as explain problems
make a distinction from similar topics
describe the historical development of Human-Machine Interaction (HMI) and apply insights from the past to future developments
list and compare various 2D input and output devices for Human-Machine Interaction
reproduce and evaluate both the potential and problems of 3D input and output devices
assess which hardware/technology is most suitable for solving specific tasks

syllabus_topics: Introduction and Motivation: Basic concepts/understanding and terminology of Human-Machine Interaction, problems of the field, historical overview

2D Input Devices: Design requirements for input devices (ISO 9241-410), value transducers, keyboards, mouse, light pen, touchscreen technologies (optical, acoustic, capacitive, resistive, inductive), Fat-Finger and Midas-Touch problem, handwriting input, optical input (cameras, scanners, eye tracking), acoustic input (microphones, speech recognition/control), haptic/tactile input, bio- and neurosensors

2D Output Devices: Visual displays (visual perception, curved/tiled displays, Edge Blending), auditory displays (auditory perception, spatial hearing, earcons/lyricons), haptic displays (tactile perception, Force Feedback, motion platforms), olfactory displays (smell perception, scent machines)
3D Input/Output Devices: 3D-mice, data gloves, LeapMotion, optical, magnetic tracking systems (Inside-out, Outside-in)
3D Input/Output Devices: Infrared-based tracking (depth camera): Kinect, gesture interaction
3D display technologies (stereoscopic, volume/holographic), Head-Mounted Displays (HMD), Oculus Rift, contact lenses as display
assessment_rules: For participants from UXD: The associated internship UXD_TMIP must be successfully completed to be eligible for the lecture exam.
